v1.name: V1 readiness
v1.summary: Premium website-first SelfOperate can support controlled pilots, but website-engine recovery/reliability still needs repeated end-to-end proof before V1 is fully ready.

v2.name: V2 readiness
v2.summary: Core integrations, workers, orchestration, ownership and recurring-operation foundations exist, but breadth of repeatedly proven real operations across the five workers and multiple business types is still incomplete.

v3.name: V3 / Full 10/10 vision
v3.summary: The full vision is materially advanced in websites, business understanding and customer infrastructure, but complete SaaS delivery, automated custom-agent creation, measured economics and near-zero founder intervention remain major gaps.

autonomyProof.note: Individual autonomous worker and acceptance proofs exist, but no representative denominator is tracked yet.

founderWorkload.note: Current automation exists, but Darius minutes versus customer-required, specialist and operator/contractor work are not measured consistently.

dimensions.name: Business understanding & scope selection
dimensions.blocker: Broad real-customer classification and scoping evidence is still limited across varied businesses.
dimensions.nextMilestone: Blind-test 20 varied businesses with no unsupported paid scope accepted.

dimensions.name: Premium website delivery
dimensions.blocker: The AWS builder still has unresolved recovery, fencing, image-settlement and final-artifact proof gaps under realistic failure conditions.
dimensions.nextMilestone: Complete 3 consecutive website journeys from directions through revision and handoff with no manual rescue.

dimensions.name: Complete SaaS & existing-app engineering
dimensions.blocker: SelfOperate does not yet have a productized governed workflow that delivers complete customer SaaS applications end to end.
dimensions.nextMilestone: Deliver one bounded app type with frontend, backend, database, auth, tests and deployment through a customer-facing workflow.

dimensions.name: Standard AI workforce capability
dimensions.blocker: Maya, Jordan, Avery, Alex and Richard have uneven real provider-backed action depth and repeated outcome proof.
dimensions.nextMilestone: Have all five workers complete at least one meaningful approved real-provider workflow with recorded outcomes.

dimensions.name: Automated custom-agent delivery
dimensions.blocker: The custom-agent offer/request path is not yet an automated agent-building and verification system.
dimensions.nextMilestone: Complete one custom agent through scope, build, independent test, practice mode, activation, monitoring and handoff.

dimensions.name: Autonomous coordination & recovery
dimensions.blocker: Recovery foundations are strong, but realistic website failure cases still expose stalls, stale ownership and manual-repair risk.
dimensions.nextMilestone: Pass kill/restart/provider-failure tests without duplicate work, lost progress or manual repair.

dimensions.name: Reliability, security & ongoing maintenance
dimensions.blocker: Restore proof, incident/alerting coverage, scale/concurrency evidence and website-engine recovery are not yet complete.
dimensions.nextMilestone: Complete a timed restore drill and a clean multi-copy failure/soak run on the current deployed stack.

dimensions.name: Complete customer journey & ownership
dimensions.blocker: Ownership and handoff are well designed, but repeated real paid journeys through final delivery, support and independent-operation handoff are not yet proven.
dimensions.nextMilestone: Complete 3 paid-like journeys including revision, support and exit/handoff with export/ownership checks.

dimensions.name: Commercial delivery & acquisition readiness
dimensions.blocker: Checkout and product infrastructure are strong, but repeatable acquisition, measured CAC and dependable real-customer conversion are not yet demonstrated.
dimensions.nextMilestone: Measure the first complete traffic → qualified intake → paid order funnel with source attribution.

dimensions.name: Economic proof & low-founder-workload operation
dimensions.blocker: There is no representative paid cohort with measured margins, retries, support burden, retention and Darius intervention hours.
dimensions.nextMilestone: Measure the first 5 paid deliveries with total spend, retries, support minutes, contractor/operator minutes and Darius minutes.

v1Remaining: Prove the AWS website builder across repeated realistic failure/recovery conditions.
Complete repeated purchase → directions → selection → build → revision → verification → deployment/handoff journeys without hidden manual rescue.
Demonstrate support/recovery behavior for failed or stalled website jobs and preserve spend/progress correctly.
v2Remaining: Give Maya, Jordan, Avery, Alex and Richard each repeated useful provider-backed operating workflows with honest capability boundaries.
Prove recurring SelfOperate operation across several supported business types, not a single archetype.
Finish dependable monitoring, restore/incident handling and customer ownership/exit paths for what V2 sells.
Measure and materially reduce Darius/operator intervention across representative customer journeys.
biggestChange: The scoring rubric has changed from launch-readiness-heavy Business Builder scoring to explicit V1, V2 and V3 milestones. Nothing became less capable because of this migration; the lower V3 progress index reflects that complete SaaS delivery, automated custom-agent construction, measured economics and near-zero founder workload are now correctly included in the end goal. Current execution evidence also shows website-builder recovery/reliability remains the highest-priority V1 proof gap.
improvements: Business understanding, payments, Founder Actions, verification, ownership/export and worker/runtime foundations are substantially implemented.
The directly integrated website engine has continued improving leases, parallel direction handling, imagery delivery, human-stop projection and calibrated scoring.
Recent Business Builder main work makes worker and provider capability claims more honest and improves dashboard/runtime behavior.
regressions: Realistic AWS website runs exposed recovery, fencing, image-settlement and stale-worker failure modes that reduce confidence in unattended V1 website completion.
Founder workload reduction remains unverified because intervention minutes are not systematically measured.
nextActions: Land and prove the website-builder repair stack, then complete 3 clean end-to-end website journeys with failure injection.
Instrument Darius, operator/contractor, customer-required and autonomous minutes/actions on every full journey.
After website reliability is proven, prove one bounded V2 operating slice repeatedly across multiple businesses before expanding into V3 SaaS/custom-agent work.
promisesOverreach: Any implication that SelfOperate can already build arbitrary complete SaaS products exceeds demonstrated capability.
Any implication that the custom-agent request path is already an automated end-to-end agent factory exceeds demonstrated capability.
Any implication that 95–99% autonomous completion or 1–2 Darius hours/week is already measured exceeds current evidence.
founderWorkloadTrend: Unknown: automation is increasing, but without measured Darius/operator/customer hours it is not possible to distinguish true workload reduction from work shifting elsewhere.

assumptions: Website reliability becomes consistently sellable within roughly 30 days.
SelfOperate receives about 150–500 qualified prospects/visitors over 90 days.
Supervised delivery capacity remains roughly 2–4 projects per month.
Roughly half to three-quarters of eligible delivered customers retain the $299/month ongoing SelfOperate service after any included period.
businessOutlook.note: One-time website/business build revenue is excluded from MRR.

costReporting.note: No consolidated representative cost dataset was available in this assessment; do not combine overlapping estimates.

method: New V1/V2/V3 baseline. SelfOperate-only assessment grounded in canonical businessbuilder main, directly integrated Stromation website-engine evidence, live/deployment records available in repositories, open PR status, recent test/synthetic journey evidence and current commercial/customer-operation truth. Open PRs receive no implemented-capability credit. Merged code is distinguished from deployed and repeatedly proven behavior. Unrelated Stromation ventures are excluded.
